objective: Both use a thin blade beneath fragile baked food, but the candidate rotates one pizza in place inside an oven while PR-2311 transfers four cookies from a sheet pan to a cooling rack.
physical_skill: Both test blade insertion beneath food without direct gripper contact or damage. The candidate additionally requires long-handle control, repeated tangential traction, continuous stone support, center correction, and confined withdrawal; PR-2311 requires lifting, level carrying, wire-rack placement, and repeated pickup cycles.
success_condition: Candidate requires a released 150–210° turn with ≤50 mm center excursion and no loss of deck contact. PR-2311 awards per-cookie placement on the rack, penalizes breakage, touch, or drops, and reserves full credit for restoring the pan and turner and clearing the scene.
reason: Thin-blade entry is genuine shared subskill, but the tested abilities and outcomes diverge materially between support-preserving in-place rotation and unsupported transfer with precise placement.
